# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Yang_2024_ganciclovir"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Yang_2024_ganciclovir"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00525-24>
* Supplement: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00525-24> (file `aac.00525-24-s0001.docx`:
  Tables S1-S8, Figures S1-S5)

# Population

Yang 2024 is a retrospective therapeutic-drug-monitoring audit of
immunocompromised children (haematological or solid-organ malignancy,
haematopoietic stem cell or solid-organ transplant, primary immunodeficiency,
or systemic immunosuppression) given intravenous ganciclovir (GCV) or enteral
valganciclovir (VGCV) for CMV prophylaxis or treatment at the Royal Children's
Hospital Melbourne and Queensland Children's Hospital Brisbane, Australia,
between April 2018 and January 2023. Neonates with congenital CMV were excluded.

After removing 15 samples below the 0.2 mg/L quantification limit, 161 serum
concentrations from 23 children were modelled (Table 1): 11 girls and 12 boys,
median age 9.0 years (range 0.4-17.0), median weight 28.2 kg (5.6-73.3),
median baseline serum creatinine 30 umol/L (19-167). Thirteen children received
IV GCV only, one enteral VGCV only and nine both; 113 samples followed GCV and
48 followed VGCV. The standard GCV regimen is 5 mg/kg twice daily as a 1-h
infusion (median given 5 mg/kg/dose, range 0.6-10.9); median VGCV dose 17.8
mg/kg/dose (6.0-47.4). Four children received renal replacement therapy at
some point. Sampling was routine TDM: a trough 0.5-1 h before a dose and a
peak 1-4 h after it.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Yang_2024_ganciclovir")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing at its source. They are
collected here.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at 70 kg, SCR 30 umol/L) | 14.1 L/h | Table 3 (RSE 9%); Table S3 final-model column |
| `lvc` (V at 70 kg) | 62.5 L | Table 3 (RSE 4%); Table S3 |
| `lka` (Ka) | 0.66 1/h | Table 3 (RSE 25%); Table S3 (0.660) |
| `lfdepot` (F, fixed) | 0.536 | Table 3 'bF 0.536 FIX'; Results: value from Acosta et al. and includes the 0.72 GCV/VGCV molecular-weight ratio |
| `e_creat_cl` | 0.997 | Table 3 'effect of SCR on CL' (RSE 7%) |
| `e_wt_cl` (fixed) | 0.75 | Table 3 'effect of weight on CL 0.75 FIX' |
| `e_wt_vc` (fixed) | 1 | Table 3 'effect of weight on V 1 FIX' |
| `etalcl` variance | 0.366^2 = 0.133956 | Table 3 BSV CL 36.6% with footnote CV% = sqrt(omega^2) x 100% |
| `propSd` | 0.392 | Table 3 prop.error.sd 39.2% |
| `addSd` | 0.144 mg/L | Table 3 add.error.sd |
| `CL = 14.10 x (30/SCR)^0.997 x (weight/70)^0.75` | -- | Table 3 footnote equation |
| `V = 62.5 x weight/70` | -- | Table 3 footnote equation |
| One compartment, first-order absorption and elimination | -- | Results 'Final population pharmacokinetic model'; supplement population-PK results (one- vs two-compartment AIC) |
| No IIV on V, Ka or F | -- | Supplement population-PK results ('the data did not provide sufficient information to estimate IIV for ... V, F, and ... Ka') |
| Combined residual error | -- | Methods; supplement population-PK results |
| SCR time-varying | -- | Methods 'SCR was tested a priori as a time-varying covariate' |

# Dosing convention

IV GCV doses are given into `central` as milligrams of ganciclovir. Enteral
VGCV doses are given into `depot` as **milligrams of valganciclovir**: the fixed
bioavailability 0.536 already contains the 0.72 GCV/VGCV molecular-weight ratio
(absolute bioavailability 0.536 / 0.72 = 0.744, Results).

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Yang_2024_ganciclovir")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
```

# Typical patient

Figure 3 uses a typical patient of 28.2 kg with serum creatinine 30 umol/L. At
5 mg/kg twice daily the steady-state AUC over 24 h is 2 x dose / CL.

```{r typical-patient}
th <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta
cl_typ <- exp(th[["lcl"]]) * (30 / 30)^th[["e_creat_cl"]] * (28.2 / 70)^th[["e_wt_cl"]]
auc_typ <- 2 * 5 * 28.2 / cl_typ
c(CL_L_per_h = cl_typ, AUC24_mg_h_per_L = auc_typ)
```

The typical value (`r round(auc_typ, 1)` mg*h/L) is close to the median post hoc
AUC24 of 38.3 mg*h/L the paper reports for its 23 children on standard dosing
(Results, Drug exposure).

# Replicate Table S4: individual exposure on standard dosing

Table S4 lists, for each of the 23 children, age, weight, serum creatinine, the
GCV dose given and the post hoc steady-state AUC24. The typical-value model is
solved for each child to steady state; `cl` is read from the solve and AUC24 is
`2 x dose / cl`. The ratio of the typical-value AUC24 to the post hoc AUC24 is
`exp(eta_CL)` for that child (up to time-varying creatinine), so its median
should sit near 1 and its log-scale spread near the 36.6% BSV, shrunk by the
10% eta shrinkage.

```{r table-s4}
# Table S4 (supplement). The source numbers the 22nd child '21' again; it is
# renumbered 22 here.
table_s4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~age,   ~WT,   ~CREAT, ~dose, ~auc_posthoc,
  1,   4,      16,    26,     80,    30.9,
  2,   4,      16.2,  30,     81,    39.1,
  3,   0.4216, 6.9,   22,     34,    17.3,
  4,   17,     69.4,  73,     347,   63.3,
  5,   13,     73.3,  150,    366,   346.6,
  6,   11,     31.7,  30,     158,   36.5,
  7,   9,      25.4,  60,     127,   52.7,
  8,   9,      35.7,  28,     178,   33.9,
  9,   9,      30.9,  93,     154,   95.8,
  10,  10,     28.2,  39,     141,   48.8,
  11,  9,      32.3,  32,     162,   33.9,
  12,  5,      26.5,  149,    132,   172.2,
  13,  3,      13.7,  20,     68,    26.7,
  14,  14,     50.6,  21,     253,   31.8,
  15,  2,      13.2,  22,     66,    34.3,
  16,  9,      28.6,  19,     143,   24.6,
  17,  0.42,   5.61,  23,     28,    38.3,
  18,  9,      19.94, 34,     100,   40.4,
  19,  10,     37.7,  83,     188,   169.5,
  20,  2,      12,    30,     60,    31.6,
  21,  16,     67.8,  167,    339,   471,
  22,  2,      11.95, 30,     60,    37.2,
  23,  14,     67.8,  97,     339,   73.9
)

ev_s4 <- table_s4 |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time = 0, evid = 1, amt = dose, rate = dose, cmt = "central", WT, CREAT) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    table_s4 |> dplyr::transmute(id, time = 1, evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central", WT, CREAT)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_s4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_s4) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl)

s4_cmp <- table_s4 |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_s4, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_typical = 2 * dose / cl,
    ratio = auc_typical / auc_posthoc
  )

s4_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(id, age, WT, CREAT, dose, cl, auc_typical, auc_posthoc, ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Child" = id, "Age (y)" = age, "WT (kg)" = WT, "SCR (umol/L)" = CREAT,
    "Dose (mg)" = dose, "Typical CL (L/h)" = cl,
    "Typical AUC24 (mg*h/L)" = auc_typical,
    "Post hoc AUC24, Table S4 (mg*h/L)" = auc_posthoc,
    "Typical / post hoc" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value AUC24 for the Table S4 children against the published post hoc AUC24.")

s4_summary <- c(
  median_ratio = median(s4_cmp$ratio),
  sd_log_ratio = sd(log(s4_cmp$ratio)),
  median_auc_typical = median(s4_cmp$auc_typical),
  median_auc_posthoc = median(s4_cmp$auc_posthoc)
)
s4_summary

# Deterministic (no random draws): a mis-transcribed CL, creatinine exponent or
# weight scaling moves the median ratio far from 1 and the spread far from the
# BSV. Measured: median ratio 1.020, SD of log ratio 0.337.
stopifnot(
  abs(s4_summary[["median_ratio"]] - 1) < 0.1,
  s4_summary[["sd_log_ratio"]] > 0.2,
  s4_summary[["sd_log_ratio"]] < 0.45
)
```

The typical-value AUC24 tracks the published post hoc AUC24 across a 20-fold
range (17 to 471 mg*h/L); the residual scatter is the individual clearance
deviations the post hoc estimates carry.

# Replicate Table 4: the optimized regimen

Table 4 recommends a twice-daily mg/kg dose for each age band and normal-range
serum creatinine band. The typical-value AUC24 at the mid-point of each band
(weight from the age-weight relation described under Assumptions) is computed
for the optimized and the standard (5 mg/kg) regimen.

```{r table-4}
wt_for_age <- function(age) 1.138805 + 3.823149 * age

table_4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~age_band,     ~age_lo, ~age_hi, ~scr_lo, ~scr_hi, ~dose_opt, ~pta_opt, ~pta_std,
  "1-4 years",   1,       4,       10,      30,      13,        61.0,     7.8,
  "1-4 years",   1,       4,       30,      50,      7,         75.3,     51.7,
  "4-10 years",  4,       10,      20,      40,      7,         67.5,     43.7,
  "4-10 years",  4,       10,      40,      60,      5,         75.7,     77.1,
  "10-16 years", 10,      16,      30,      60,      5,         74.3,     72.4,
  "10-16 years", 10,      16,      60,      80,      3,         76.3,     47.2,
  "16-18 years", 16,      18,      50,      80,      3,         78.1,     45.3,
  "16-18 years", 16,      18,      80,      110,     2,         77.7,     13.0
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    row = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT = wt_for_age((age_lo + age_hi) / 2),
    CREAT = (scr_lo + scr_hi) / 2
  )

ev_t4 <- table_4 |>
  dplyr::transmute(id = row, time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central", WT, CREAT)
cl_t4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_t4) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::select(id, cl)

t4_cmp <- table_4 |>
  dplyr::left_join(cl_t4, by = c("row" = "id")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_opt = 2 * dose_opt * WT / cl,
    auc_std = 2 * 5 * WT / cl
  )

t4_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(scr_band = paste0(scr_lo, "-", scr_hi)) |>
  dplyr::select(age_band, scr_band, WT, CREAT, dose_opt, auc_opt, pta_opt, auc_std, pta_std) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age" = age_band, "SCR band (umol/L)" = scr_band, "WT used (kg)" = WT,
    "SCR used (umol/L)" = CREAT, "Optimized dose (mg/kg bid)" = dose_opt,
    "Typical AUC24, optimized" = auc_opt, "Published PTA, optimized (%)" = pta_opt,
    "Typical AUC24, 5 mg/kg" = auc_std, "Published PTA, 5 mg/kg (%)" = pta_std
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value AUC24 (mg*h/L) at the mid-point of each Table 4 band.")

# Deterministic. The optimized regimen was chosen to hit 40-100 mg*h/L, so its
# typical AUC24 sits inside the window in every band (measured 54-69). Where the
# paper reports a standard-dose PTA below 20% (rows 1 and 8), the typical
# standard-dose AUC24 falls outside the window (measured 20.7 and 154).
stopifnot(
  all(t4_cmp$auc_opt > 40 & t4_cmp$auc_opt < 100),
  t4_cmp$auc_std[1] < 40,
  t4_cmp$auc_std[8] > 100
)
```

# Replicate Figure 4 / Table S5: exposure by age group

Figure 4 and Table S5 summarise simulated AUC24 for 703 children from a hospital
covariate database, by age group with age-specific normal serum creatinine. The
database is not published, so 200 children per age group are drawn here with
age uniform over the band, weight from the age-weight relation and serum
creatinine uniform over the normal range printed under each Figure 4 group.
The spread of the published boxes is consistent with typical-value simulation,
so between-subject variability is switched off.

```{r figure-4}
fig4_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~age_group,    ~age_lo, ~age_hi, ~scr_lo, ~scr_hi, ~pub_median, ~pub_p05, ~pub_p95,
  "1-4 years",   1,       4,       10,      50,      25.8,        18.2,     46.2,
  "4-10 years",  4,       10,      20,      60,      44.5,        28.1,     69.2,
  "10-16 years", 10,      16,      30,      80,      65.3,        46.4,     107.6,
  "16-18 years", 16,      18,      50,      110,     99.65,       78.1,     145.3
)

set.seed(20240917)
cohort_fig4 <- fig4_groups |>
  dplyr::mutate(grp = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    age_group = age_group,
    age = runif(200, age_lo, age_hi),
    CREAT = runif(200, scr_lo, scr_hi),
    .by = grp
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), WT = wt_for_age(age))

# Optimized dose by age band and creatinine sub-band (Table 4).
opt_dose <- function(age, scr) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    age < 4 ~ ifelse(scr < 30, 13, 7),
    age < 10 ~ ifelse(scr < 40, 7, 5),
    age < 16 ~ ifelse(scr < 60, 5, 3),
    TRUE ~ ifelse(scr < 80, 3, 2)
  )
}

ev_fig4 <- cohort_fig4 |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central", WT, CREAT)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_fig4$id))
cl_fig4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_fig4) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::select(id, cl)

auc_fig4 <- cohort_fig4 |>
  dplyr::left_join(cl_fig4, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `5 mg/kg twice daily` = 2 * 5 * WT / cl,
    `Optimized regimen (Table 4)` = 2 * opt_dose(age, CREAT) * WT / cl,
    age_group = factor(age_group, levels = fig4_groups$age_group)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`5 mg/kg twice daily`, `Optimized regimen (Table 4)`),
                      names_to = "regimen", values_to = "auc24")

ggplot(auc_fig4, aes(age_group, auc24)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outlier.size = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(40, 100), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUCss,24h (mg*h/L)",
       title = "Simulated steady-state AUC24 by age group, normal serum creatinine",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Yang 2024 (covariate distributions approximated; see text).")

auc_fig4 |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "5 mg/kg twice daily") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_median = median(auc24),
    sim_p05 = quantile(auc24, 0.05),
    sim_p95 = quantile(auc24, 0.95),
    sim_pct_target = 100 * mean(auc24 >= 40 & auc24 <= 100),
    .by = age_group
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig4_groups |> dplyr::select(age_group, pub_median, pub_p05, pub_p95), by = "age_group") |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age group" = age_group, "Simulated median" = sim_median,
    "Simulated P5" = sim_p05, "Simulated P95" = sim_p95,
    "Simulated % in 40-100" = sim_pct_target,
    "Table S5 median" = pub_median, "Table S5 P5" = pub_p05, "Table S5 P95" = pub_p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Standard dosing (5 mg/kg twice daily): simulated vs Table S5 AUC24 (mg*h/L).")
```

The rise of exposure with age on standard mg/kg dosing, and its flattening
under the optimized regimen, are reproduced. The simulated medians run about
15-40% above Table S5 because a uniform draw over each printed creatinine range
places more children at the top of the range than the hospital database the
paper resampled (AUC24 is almost proportional to serum creatinine). No gate is
placed on this comparison for that reason; the deterministic checks above carry
the validation.

# Steady-state profiles and PKNCA

A cohort of 200 children per arm, with (weight, creatinine) pairs resampled from
Table S4 and between-subject variability on CL, receives either IV GCV 5 mg/kg
as a 1-h infusion or enteral VGCV 17.8 mg/kg (the Table 1 median) every 12 h for
10 days. PKNCA computes AUC over the final dosing interval, which at steady
state equals `F x dose / CL` for each child.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20240917)
set.seed(20240917)
n_arm <- 200
make_arm <- function(arm, id_offset) {
  pick <- sample(nrow(table_s4), n_arm, replace = TRUE)
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_arm),
    arm = arm,
    WT = table_s4$WT[pick],
    CREAT = table_s4$CREAT[pick]
  )
}
cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_arm("IV GCV 5 mg/kg", 0L),
  make_arm("Enteral VGCV 17.8 mg/kg", n_arm)
)

dose_times <- seq(0, 228, by = 12)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 216, by = 4), seq(228, 240, by = 0.25))))

doses <- cohort |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = dose_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    evid = 1,
    amt = ifelse(arm == "IV GCV 5 mg/kg", 5, 17.8) * WT,
    rate = ifelse(arm == "IV GCV 5 mg/kg", amt, 0),
    cmt = ifelse(arm == "IV GCV 5 mg/kg", "central", "depot")
  )
obs <- cohort |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = obs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm"), maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

```{r profiles}
# Steady-state interval 228-240 h; sampling windows used for TDM in the paper
# are shaded (trough 0.5-1 h pre-dose, peak 1-4 h post-dose).
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 228) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 228) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .by = c(arm, tad)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 1, xmax = 4, ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "darkgreen") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 11, xmax = 11.5, ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "darkblue") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Serum ganciclovir (mg/L)",
       title = "Steady-state profiles: median and 90% interval",
       caption = "Illustrative; the paper's Figure 2 VPC is over time since first dose of the observed TDM data.")
```

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  doses |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm),
  amt ~ time | arm + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 228, end = 240, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

f_vgcv <- exp(rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta[["lfdepot"]])
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    doses |> dplyr::filter(time == 228) |> dplyr::select(id, amt, arm),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_closed = ifelse(arm == "IV GCV 5 mg/kg", 1, f_vgcv) * amt / cl) |>
  dplyr::left_join(nca_wide |> dplyr::select(id, auclast), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast - auc_closed) / auc_closed)

# Same drawn parameters on both sides, so the difference is trapezoidal error
# on a 0.25-h grid plus residual accumulation after 10 days.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(indiv$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(indiv$pct_diff), 0.9) < 3
)

indiv |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median AUC24 (mg*h/L)` = median(2 * auclast),
    `P5 AUC24` = quantile(2 * auclast, 0.05),
    `P95 AUC24` = quantile(2 * auclast, 0.95),
    `% with AUC24 40-100` = 100 * mean(2 * auclast >= 40 & 2 * auclast <= 100),
    `Median |PKNCA - closed form| (%)` = median(abs(pct_diff)),
    .by = arm
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Steady-state AUC24 (2 x AUC over the last 12-h interval) from PKNCA.")
```

## Comparison against published exposure

The paper reports no NCA; its exposure summary is the post hoc AUC24 on
standard dosing (median 38.3 mg*h/L, 5th-95th percentile 24.8-329.2, Results).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,             ~auclast,
  "IV GCV 5 mg/kg", 38.3 / 2
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "IV arm: simulated median AUC over a 12-h interval at steady state vs half the published median post hoc AUC24. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

The simulated cohort resamples the same 23 children's weight and creatinine,
so its median AUC24 lands near the published post hoc median.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Weight for age.** The paper derived simulated children's weights from "the
  observed correlation between weight and age within our patient cohort"
  without printing the relation. A straight line fitted by the maintainers to
  the Table S4 ages and weights (WT = 1.139 + 3.823 x age, kg and years) is
  used. With mg/kg dosing, AUC24 depends on weight only as WT^0.25, so this
  choice barely affects any result above.
- **Serum creatinine distributions** for Figure 4 / Table S5 come from an
  unpublished hospital database; uniform draws over the printed normal ranges
  are used, which biases the simulated medians upward (see the Figure 4
  section).
- **Table S4** gives the 22nd child the number 21 (a duplicate); it is
  renumbered 22. Its serum creatinine is presumably the baseline value, whereas
  the post hoc AUC used the time-varying value.
- **Valganciclovir dose units.** Enteral doses are milligrams of
  valganciclovir into `depot`; the fixed F = 0.536 includes the
  molecular-weight ratio, as in the source.
- **Renal replacement therapy** was tested on CL and not retained (OFV change
  0.056; Discussion), so the model has no RRT term.
- **Figure 2** (VPC over time since first dose of the TDM data) cannot be
  rebuilt without the individual dosing histories; the steady-state profile
  plot is illustrative only.
- No correction notice for the article was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-10-30.
